VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The per-file changes (Owner field + getter/setter, DeleteOwner soft-delete, schema across all four dialects, OpenAPI) are each in the right unit and read naturally. The problem is how the new "ignore soft-deleted owners" rule is placed.

**Finding 1 — the soft-delete filter is a cross-cutting rule duplicated inline rather than defined once.**
This codebase is deliberately disciplined about single-definition rules: `Household` exists so the resolver, duplicate gate and builder "all agree" on the id, and `PossibleDuplicate` is the "canonical soft-match rule … defined once so the create and fetch pipelines agree." Against that grain, the new rule is copy-pasted as an inline `if (existing.isDeleted()) continue;` into two separate `ownerRepository.findAll()` loops (`PossibleDuplicate.matchOf` at line 46 and `Household.hasMember` at line 79). "Ignore soft-deleted owners when scanning owners" is exactly the kind of cross-pipeline predicate this codebase centralizes. It belongs in one place — e.g. a shared helper filtering the `findAll()` stream, or a repository `findAllActive()` — so every scan honors it consistently rather than each loop re-deciding.

**Finding 2 — the filter is applied inconsistently within `Household`, which is a coherence smell.**
`Household.hasMember` (line 79) now skips deleted owners, but `Household.size` (lines 101–107), which loops the very same `findAll()` by `householdId`, does not. Whether `size` *should* count deleted owners is a spec/correctness question I'm not judging — but having two sibling methods in one class scan the same collection with one honoring the deleted flag and the other silently not is precisely the inconsistency a scattered inline predicate produces, and precisely what a single shared filter (Finding 1) would prevent. A maintainer reading `Household` would not find this split natural. At minimum make the treatment uniform/explicit; better, route both through the one shared filter.

Collapsing these into a single definition would resolve both findings and match the established idiom of the module.
